movesets.name: Sticky Web
movesets.description:
Araquanid carves a niche as one of the tier's reliable Sticky Web user due to its good defensive typing, serviceable bulk, and amazing offensive matchups against notable threats to Sticky Web teams such as Iron Moth, Cinderace, Iron Treads, and Great Tusk. Surf is not only a very consistent STAB move for reliable damage, but it also prevents Glimmora from setting up Toxic Spikes via Toxic Debris and allows Araquanid to deal with Taunt Landorus-T that might try to prevent Araquanid from setting Sticky Web. With Endeavor, Araquanid can chip the notable Water-type checks of the tier like Ogerpon-W and Primarina, and using it with Custap Berry allows Araquanid to deal sudden damage to threatening sweepers such as Kyurem and Dragonite before being KOed. Endure can be used to activate Custap Berry more consistently in the face of counter leads such as Raging Bolt and powerful Choice Band users such as Zamazenta, while Lunge helps to deal with threatening anti-leads like Ogerpon-W and opposing leads like Hisuian Samurott. Mirror Coat can alternatively be opted for to deal massive damage to special attackers such as Zapdos and Raging Bolt, and Leech Life is a similar option to Lunge to deal with opposing leads, trading a helpful Attack drop for some much-appreciated recovery. Although Custap Berry almost guarantees that Araquanid will find an additional turn on lead, Mental Herb is an alternative that ensures Araquanid can set up Sticky Web in the face of Taunt users like Landorus-T and Deoxys-S. 40 Defense EVs and maximum HP investment guarantees Araquanid will take two Ceaseless Edges from Hisuian Samurott, and a Modest nature with the rest of its remaining EVs in Special Attack will enable Araquanid to 2HKO physically defensive Hatterene with Surf even after Leftovers recovery. An alternative and more defensive EV spread of 252 HP / 4 Atk / 136 Def / 4 SpA / 112 SpD with a Sassy nature is also an option; this specially defensive spread allows it to survive a Thunderbolt from Protosynthesis Raging Bolt, while 4 EVs in Attack guarantee a 2HKO on Ogerpon-W with Lunge, and 4 Special Attack EVs ensure an OHKO against offensive Great Tusk with Surf. The remaining EVs are invested into Defense to improve the matchup against opposing leads like Hisuian Samurott. Araquanid can also invest 28 EVs into Speed to outpace Ting-Lu. Alternatively, sets with a Speed-lowering nature can drop their Speed IVs to 28 to underspeed Garganacl and Toxapex, allowing Araquanid to weaken them with Endeavor after they use Recover, just before it faints to Salt Cure or Toxic. Although Terastallizing Araquanid should generally be avoided in order to preserve Terastallization for offensive teammates that generally take advantage of it more, Tera Ghost allows Araquanid to spinblock Iron Treads and Great Tusk in emergencies to guarantee Sticky Web stays up and also allows Araquanid to get a guaranteed Endeavor off against Extreme Speed Dragonite if it is in Custap Berry activation range.

Araquanid has found its home as a reliable entry hazard setter on Sticky Web hyper offense teams, and as such, setup sweepers with middling Speed tiers greatly appreciate its presence. Gholdengo is an almost-required teammate on such structures and allows Sticky Web teams to block hazard removal from Rapid Spin, Glimmora's Mortal Spin, and Defog thanks to its ability. Gholdengo is also invaluable in dismantling the bulkier team structures that hyper offense teams in general struggle against greatly. Other Ghost-types such as Pecharunt and Ceruledge also block Rapid Spin attempts, with Pecharunt's bulk proving valuable against the likes of Zamazenta and Ogerpon-W, while Ceruledge offers extra speed support thanks to Weak Armor. Setup sweepers with middling Speed tiers such as Attack Booster Energy Great Tusk, Raging Bolt, and Meteor Beam Glimmora also pair excellently with Araquanid. Great Tusk’s hazard removal can allow Araquanid to come in multiple times per match, and its typing allows for it to check anti-leads to Araquanid, namely Raging Bolt. Iron Treads can also be considered on Sticky Web teams heavily weak to Raging Bolt. Meteor Beam Glimmora can assist Sticky Web structures by absorbing Toxic Spikes and setting Stealth Rock for its teammates while also still maintaining heavy offensive pressure. Iron Moth is another potent sweeper that Sticky Web teams can employ, as Sticky Web being set up lets Iron Moth run maximum Special Attack investment and a Modest nature, granting it a Special Attack boost from its Booster Energy and allowing it to do more consistent damage even without boosts from Fiery Dance. Kingambit can also take great advantage of Sticky Web, as it allows for Kingambit to get the jump on opposing Jolly Kingambit and, if Kingambit itself opts to run a Jolly nature, maximum Speed Great Tusk without Heavy-Duty Boots. Ogerpon-W is excellent on Sticky Web teams, as with Swords Dance and an Adamant nature, which it can now run thanks to Araquanid relieving it from the pressure of Speed ties with opposing Ogerpon-W, it forms a strong core with Gholdengo that can throttle the bulkier team structures that hyper offense teams tend to struggle with.

movesets.name: Sticky Web (Bug)
movesets.description:
Araquanid makes for a good Sticky Web setter for Bug teams due to having more bulk than other Sticky Web setters, such as Galvantula and Ribombee, as well as being a huge asset to Bug teams with its Water Bubble ability, resisting Fire-type moves and hitting Fire-type Pokemon super effectively. Liquidation is a strong STAB move capable of 2HKOing common entry hazard removers such as Great Tusk and Iron Treads. Infestation helps trap and check Pokemon, such as Ting Lu and Klefki. Mirror Coat is used to take advantage of Araquanid's naturally good special bulk to OHKO threats such as Raging Bolt and Zapdos.

Choice Scarf Kleavor is a great teammate for Araquanid because it can deal with Fire- and Flying-types such as Ogerpon-H, Moltres, and Articuno. Kleavor's Stone Axe also synergizes nicely with Araquanid’s Sticky Web, as more entry hazards further help the sweepers and wallbreakers on the team while also breaking Ceruledge's Focus Sash, which would otherwise be a huge problem for Bug teams. Scizor is another great teammate for Araquanid, as Sticky Web enables it to set up with Swords Dance easier and also allows it to take out Iron Treads Bisharp, and Choice Band Hisuian Arcanine. Volcarona also benefits from Sticky Web, as it outspeeds faster threats like Greninja and Iron Valiant at -1. Slither Wing and Lokix both appreciate Sticky Web, as it helps them revenge kill faster threats such as Gholdengo, Ogerpon-H, and Hisuian Arcanine. Forretress provides a strong physical wall on Bug teams, removes entry hazards with Rapid Spin, and is a slow pivot for Araquanid with Volt Switch to ensure its safe entry so it can repeatedly set up Sticky Web if needed.

strategies.overview:
Draft Order: Round 7 onwards

Price Range: 5-6 points

Overview: Araquanid brings Sticky Web to a draft, offering a better defensive profile than its competition in this department. Even if it struggles to justify being brought to most matches, its defensive and offensive capabilities provide it some value to teams with strong entry hazard control and slow wallbreakers. Since it can only deal decent damage with Water-type attacks and no reliable recovery, Araquanid is often more of a threat in the teambuilder rather than a Pokemon worth bringing.
strategies.comments:
Common Roles

Sticky Web Setter: Araquanid is blessed with the limited Sticky Web, and its stats also allow it to be more than just a suicide lead to set it up, enabling it to potentially set it up multiple times over the course of a game if necessary while also being able to deal good amounts of damage to foes.

Special Tank: With a great Special Defense stat and a powerful ability in Water Bubble, Araquanid can limit the potential of specially offensive Pokemon like Volcarona and Armarouge.

Common Moves

Primary STAB Moves: Leech Life, Liquidation

Setup Moves: Iron Defense

Utility Moves: Substitute, Sticky Web, Rest, Sleep Talk, Reflect

Coverage: Crunch, Poison Jab

Niche Moves

Infestation: Araquanid can trap spinners like Iron Treads and Corviknight that switch in expecting Sticky Web, allowing defensive sets to safely remove them from the battle. Additionally, Infestation can ensure that a teammate can get in safely without the fear of a double switch.

Endure: Araquanid can serve as an emergency option to remove a dangerous sweeper, pairing with Custap Berry to ensure one turn of moving first against faster foes. Endeavor can be paired with Endure to quickly reduce a Pokemon's HP, but in many cases, Water Bubble-boosted Liquidation can deal more damage.

Pounce: Pounce can provide a surprise decrease in Speed to enable a teammate to come in more safely.

Mirror Coat: With solid Special Defense, Araquanid can take powerful hits from specially offensive foes and deal lots of damage to them in return.

Common Items

Heavy-Duty Boots: Taking outsized damage from Stealth Rock and being vulnerable to all other entry hazards, Araquanid needs Heavy-Duty Boots if it wants to switch in multiple times during a game.

Focus Sash: Araquanid's defenses are not extraordinary, meaning there are plenty of powerful attacks that can outright OHKO it. Focus Sash ensures that lead sets have a turn to set up Sticky Web or accomplish another task.

Leftovers: Araquanid can spend several turns on the battlefield, but it lacks strong recovery outside of Leech Life. Leftovers can provide passive healing to enhance its longevity.

Niche Items

Mental Herb: With low Speed, Araquanid can find itself hindered by Taunt when trying to set up Sticky Web. Mental Herb can avoid this limitation, ensuring that Sticky Web can go up at the start of the battle.

Choice Band: With a Choice Band, Araquanid can turn into a powerful wallbreaker. Liquidation backed by a Choice Band and potentially Tera can turn even resisted hits into 2HKOs. Pokemon that switch in to remove Sticky Web, such as Corviknight and Tentacruel, can be significantly weakened by a powerful Liquidation.

Red Card: With decent enough defenses, Araquanid can use Red Card to force out a boosted sweeper, and it can be paired with Endure to guarantee activation if the foe is strong enough to KO it.

Resistance Berries: With strong enough defenses to take neutral hits, Araquanid can benefit from a targeted resistance berry to survive a hit it normally wouldn't, ensuring a powerful hit back or a placing of Sticky Web.

Sitrus Berry: Araquanid is able to stomach most hits without fainting, but it can often find itself too weak after an encounter to reliably stomach further hits. Sitrus Berry can turn 2HKOs into 3HKOs, providing it with more turns on the field.

Tera

Araquanid has a satisfactory typing that does not require a Tera Captain position. However, it can make decent use of Tera in the few opportunities it may get to use it as a secondary Captain. A defensive typing that shifts its weaknesses can allow it to turn an unfavorable encounter into its favor, providing it some longevity. With Water Bubble reducing Fire-type damage, defensive types that are weak to Fire, such as Tera Steel, are even stronger. An offensive Tera type in Tera Water can be utilized to further power up its Water-type attacks, which can already be difficult for many Pokemon to safely switch in on.

Draft Strategy

Araquanid stands apart from other Sticky Web setters by providing good wallbreaking and decent defenses to a draft. Sticky Web makes a significant impact on a team's strategy, which can appreciate its other contributions as opposed to being pigeon-holed into setting up a single entry hazard once. However, as Araquanid is often difficult to bring to every single match, much of its presence is felt in the teambuilder. Teams should not be overly reliant on Sticky Web's presence, but a Sticky Web setter that doesn't fold to neutral hits is appreciated by many different Pokemon.

Wallbreakers: Pokemon like Metagross, Chi-Yu, and Great Tusk appreciate moving before their foes, further enabling them to fire off powerful attacks more freely. Additionally, faster wallbreakers like Meowscarada and Ogerpon-W appreciate Sticky Web for negating revenge killers that run Choice Scarf to outspeed them.

Swords Dance / Nasty Plot Sweepers: Sweepers that do not rely on boosting their Speed can benefit from not needing to take a faster hit every turn, hitting with boosted attacks before opposing Pokemon can even act.

Ghost-types: Araquanid has the ability to set up Sticky Web more than once, but it prefers Pokemon like Gholdengo and Gengar to entirely prevent Defog or Rapid Spin from removing it from the field.

Checks and Counters

Hazard removal: Araquanid's value is primarily Sticky Web, so Pokemon like Galarian Weezing and Iron Treads that can successfully use Defog or Rapid Spin after it has left the battlefield removes its primary contribution.

Water-resistant Pokemon: Araquanid's offensive capabilities are severely limited when it cannot deal much damage with its Water-type moves, allowing switch-ins like Volcanion, Salamence, and Palafin to hinder any progress from it on an offensive front.

Taunt / Encore: Whether it is forced to use Sticky Web multiple times or entirely prevented from using it, Araquanid can quickly become a momentum sink. Being locked into a specific attacking move can also open the door for a Pokemon that does not mind it to switch in and begin to set up.

Wallbreakers: Without good recovery and Speed, Araquanid eventually crumbles against the powerful hits from wallbreakers like Iron Hands, Tornadus-T, and Urshifu-S.

movesets.name: Sticky Web
movesets.description:
Araquanid functions as the tier's premier Sticky Web setter, leveraging its good natural bulk and access to Magic Coat to reliably get up Sticky Web while also denying entry hazards. Surf is usually used in order to OHKO Landorus-T and Great Tusk, preventing the latter from removing Sticky Web, while Liquidation hits Ting-Lu and Gliscor for greater damage. Bug Buzz and Leech Life are also both options in order to hit Ogerpon-W, which would otherwise use Araquanid as setup fodder and can give Sticky Web teams some trouble otherwise. Endure combines well with Custap Berry, allowing Araquanid to get an extra hit off on foes or potentially get Sticky Web up again against Rapid Spin or Defog users such as Great Tusk and Landorus-T. Endeavor is also an option, pairing well with Endure and Custap Berry to bring foes that resist Araquanid's Water-type attacks, such as Ferrothorn and Kyurem, down to low HP. Magic Coat is used in order to prevent hazards from foes such as Ting-Lu and Ferrothorn while also stopping Taunt from foes such as Landorus-T. 40 Defense EVs allow Araquanid to survive two of Jolly Hisuian Samurott's Ceaseless Edges from full health.

Araquanid fits solely on Sticky Web hyper offense structures. Slower wallbreakers such as Raging Bolt and Hisuian Samurott appreciate Araquanid's Sticky Web compensating for their below-average Speed stats, letting them outspeed and threaten foes such as Iron Valiant and Zamazenta. Gholdengo blocks Rapid Spin and Defog, helping to keep Sticky Web up, and benefits from Sticky Web allowing it to sweep with Nasty Plot more easily. Other setup sweepers such as Ogerpon-W and Great Tusk also appreciate the Sticky Web support Araquanid provides, preventing Pokemon such as Tapu Lele and Iron Valiant from revenge killing them as easily. As Araquanid often struggles to get Sticky Web up in the face of Mega Diancie, Flying-types such as Tornadus-T, Electric-types such as Tapu Koko, and Steel-types such as the aforementioned Gholdengo and Mega Scizor are appreciated. In return, they benefit from Sticky Web slowing down foes such as Heatran and Hisuian Samurott while also appreciating Araquanid providing a switch-in against Fire-type foes such as Heatran, Volcarona, and Cinderace.

movesets.name: Sticky Web Setter
movesets.description: Araquanid establishes itself as one of the best Sticky Web setters in the tier, finding a niche in the metagame by means of leveraging its wide support movepool to disrupt other leads and ability to threaten one of the best forms of entry hazard removal in Excadrill. When paired with Custap Berry, Endure guarantees the setting of Sticky Web, even in the face of Mega Aerodactyl and Choice Band Rillaboom threatening an OHKO. Toxic ensures Araquanid cannot be hard walled by Water-type Pokemon, namely Slowbro and Volcanion, which it would otherwise not be able to do damage to. Pounce is another option to slow down faster lead Pokemon for its teammates to exploit. Endeavor pairs nicely with Endure and Custap Berry, putting an opposing Pokemon in range to be picked off by a teammate like Aegislash and Scizor. Magic Coat turns the tables on foes like Mew attempting to either disrupt Araquanid with Taunt, preventing Sticky Web from going up, or Pokemon like Clefable and Hippowdon attempting to set up hazards. Mental Herb can be used over Custap Berry to flip the matchup against Taunt users like Mew and Serperior attempting to shut down the usage of Sticky Web. 252 HP EVs paired with 228 Defense EVs and an Impish nature allow for Araquanid to live Adamant Tyranitar's Stone Edge. Araquanid is best utilized on hyper offense teams, with Sticky Web facilitating setup sweepers and wallbreakers such as Iron Moth, Iron Boulder, Galarian Moltres, and Blacephalon by means of allowing them to outspeed faster foes and limiting opportunities to revenge kill its teammates. Serperior and Bisharp are great partners, either deterring the usage of Defog or exploiting the activation of their respective abilities to start snowballing. Ghost-types like Air Balloon Aegislash and Ghostium Z Pecharunt work as spinblockers against Excadrill, while Sticky Web makes up for their lackluster Speed stats. Mega Aerodactyl and Heavy-Duty Boots Zeraora are immune to Sticky Web, so checks for them are mandatory; Celesteela, Scizor, and Booster Energy Speed Iron Crown work well against Mega Aerodctyl, while Serperior, Rillaboom, and Sinistcha can handle Zeraora.

movesets.name: Sticky Web (Bug)
movesets.description: Araquanid is the best defensive Sticky Web setter and a staple on Bug teams, as its ability Water Bubble combined with its high Special Defense gives it valuable defensive utility against Fire-types and special attackers. Liquidation threatens Fire- and Ground-types as well as physically frail Pokemon that don't resist Water like Iron Valiant, Enamorus, and Sneasler. Toxic punishes bulky switch-ins like Mantine, Rotom-W, Porygon2, and Volcanion. Magic Coat counters entry hazards and status spread from Pokemon like Shuckle, Celesteela, and Klefki that will attempt to exploit Araquanid's passivity. Leech Life is a niche option that gives Araquanid minor recovery and threatens Pokemon like Ogerpon-W, Hydreigon, Latios, and Latias. Mirror Coat is an option for Water-resistant foes and omniboost sweepers like Pelipper, Kommo-o, and Hisuian Zoroark, as Araquanid can comfortably take an attack and OHKO them in return. The given EV spread maximizes Araquanid's bulk while also outspeeding base 50 Speed Pokemon with no investment like Ursaluna, Ting-Lu, Hippowdon, and Alolan Muk, which are all threatened by Liquidation. Araquanid synergizes best with teammates that utilize the speed control Sticky Web provides and appreciate the elimination of Pokemon it counters. Volcarona greatly benefits from the removal of Fire-types like Heatran and Victini, making the opening for a sweep easier. With the Sticky Web speed decrease, Volcarona is able to outspeed its checks after only one Quiver Dance and deals with the Grass and Electric types Araquanid is countered by. Choice Scarf Kleavor is a great Stealth Rock setter that takes out Hisuian Arcanine, provides momentum with U-turn, and benefits from Sticky Web. Strong physical attackers like Heracross, Scizor, and Mega Pinsir break walls that Araquanid can't touch like Toxapex, Tapu Fini, and Ferrothorn; they also excel with Sticky Web support, letting them set up and outspeed their checks like Kyurem, Ceruledge, and Tapu Lele.
